article.body_html:
Two days into a week-long booking, plans change: a work trip moves, a friend offers a lift north, or the weather ruins the route you had in mind. The bike is fine, but you now need it for two of the seven days. Whether the shop will take it back early is the first thing to ask. The question behind it is what happens to the five days you will not use, and the best time to ask is before the full week is paid for or, if it already is, as soon as you know your plans have changed.

Four questions inside "can I return it early?"

One sentence from a renter can hide four different questions, and a shop's answer to one says nothing about the others. Separate them before you ask.

QuestionWhy it mattersWords to use
Can the rental end early at all?A booking may be written as a fixed period, or as a start date and a return date that can move"If I bring the bike back on day 2 instead of day 7, is that acceptable?"
What happens to the unused days?They might be charged, credited, partly adjusted or simply lost, and only the shop can say which"What will I pay for the five days I will not use?"
How are days counted?A bike returned on the afternoon of day 2 may count as one day or as two"If I return at 15:00 on day 2, how many days are charged?"
What about the deposit?The deposit is separate from the rental fee and follows its own record"When and how is my deposit returned if I finish early?"

The shop's answers will depend on the booking you made and on what it agrees, so the aim is to get all four answered, not just one.

The best moment to ask is at booking

A change of plan is easier to handle when the answer already exists. When you book a week, add one line to your message: "If I need to return the bike early, what happens to the unused days?" Keep the reply with your booking record. The shop may say it does not adjust anything, or that it decides case by case. Either answer helps, because you then choose between a week and a shorter booking with the facts in front of you. A booking message template is a good place to add the question, and the guide to 50cc rental cancellations lists what to ask before you pay.

Put numbers next to the question

The size of the difference decides how hard it is worth pressing. Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà gives reference prices of 150,000 to 200,000 VND for one day and 700,000 to 800,000 VND for one week on a manual bike. For illustration, if a renter returned a manual bike after two days and the shop agreed to count those two days at the day rate, they would come to 300,000 to 400,000 VND, against 700,000 to 800,000 VND for the week. Whether a booking would ever be re-priced like that is the shop's decision, so treat the sum as a yardstick, not a quote. It only shows what is at stake: a few hundred thousand dong is worth one polite message.

If your plans change mid-rental

  1. Tell the shop as soon as you know. The shop is open 09:00–21:00 daily, so a call or message the evening before is better than a surprise at the counter.
  2. Say what you want in one sentence: the bike, the original return date, the new return date and the time you will arrive.
  3. Ask for the new total in writing, including how the unused days are treated and what, if anything, is still owed.
  4. Return the bike properly. The return checklist covers the receipt and handover, and the guide to recording a deposit covers payment and return.
  5. Keep the closing message. A line from the shop confirming the return date, the amount paid and that nothing else is owed is worth more than a memory of a conversation.

The one confirmed rule is about extra time

Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà has confirmed one rule about adding time: an extension costs 20,000 VND per hour, and more than 6 hours is charged as one rental day. That says how extra hours are priced, not how an early return is counted. It says nothing about unused days, so do not read it as a promise of anything in that direction; if anything, it is a reason to ask how a return time is counted.

A message to send

When you contact the shop, include these points:

  • the bike, the booking dates and the day you now plan to return it;
  • a request to say how the unused days will be treated and what you will pay in total;
  • a request to say how a return time on that day is counted;
  • a question about when and how your deposit comes back;
  • a request to put the answer in a message you can keep.

The shop's FAQ page collects its answers to questions about renting in Hanoi. If your plans change, the number to call is 0334 699 969, between 09:00 and 21:00 daily.
